_comment: Each benchmark is implemented in five languages (Cangjie/C++/Rust/Go/Python).
Each implementation prints exactly two trailing lines to stdout:
The runner verifies CHECKSUM is identical across implementations of the
same benchmark, and uses ELAPSED_MS as the measurement.
Sizes are chosen so the full suite finishes in roughly one minute on a
modern laptop. Override per-benchmark via 'sizes' in this file or via

benchmarks.name: fibonacci
benchmarks.title: Recursive Fibonacci (function call / recursion)
benchmarks.description: Pure recursive fib(N). Stresses function-call overhead and integer arithmetic. No standard-library involvement beyond integers.

benchmarks.name: sort
benchmarks.title: Sort 2M integers (stdlib sort)
benchmarks.description: Generate 2,000,000 deterministic pseudo-random Int64 values then sort ascending using the language's standard sort. Stresses standard library sorting and dynamic arrays.

benchmarks.name: hashmap_ops
benchmarks.title: HashMap insert + lookup (stdlib hash table)
benchmarks.description: Insert N (string,int) pairs then look up the same N keys. Stresses hash maps, string hashing, and string allocation.

benchmarks.name: string_concat
benchmarks.title: String building (stdlib StringBuilder)
benchmarks.description: Build a single large string from N small fragments using the recommended efficient builder for each language. Stresses string buffers and memory growth.

benchmarks.name: closure_sum
benchmarks.title: Closure / higher-order pipeline
benchmarks.description: Apply a map -> filter -> reduce pipeline of closures over N integers. Stresses higher-order function dispatch, closure allocation, and integer arithmetic.

benchmarks.name: enum_eval
benchmarks.title: Enum / pattern matching (AST evaluation)
benchmarks.description: Build a recursive arithmetic expression tree of depth D and evaluate it N times via recursive pattern matching on a sum-type enum (Num | Add | Sub | Mul). Stresses algebraic data types, recursive calls, and tag dispatch.

benchmarks.name: regex_search
benchmarks.title: Regex find-all (stdlib regex)
benchmarks.description: Run a non-trivial alternation regex (date | email | capitalized word) across REPEATS copies of a sample paragraph. Stresses the standard regex engine.

benchmarks.name: math_loop
benchmarks.title: Math-intensive loop (sin/cos/sqrt/exp)
benchmarks.description: Sum sin(x)*cos(x)+sqrt(x+1)-exp(-x) over N points. Stresses the math standard library and floating-point throughput.

benchmarks.name: prime_sieve
benchmarks.title: Sieve of Eratosthenes
benchmarks.description: Classic Sieve of Eratosthenes up to N on a one-byte-per-cell boolean array, then count primes and sum them mod 2^31. Algorithmically identical across all three languages: same loop bounds, same inner stride, same checksum formula.

benchmarks.name: quicksort
benchmarks.title: Hand-written quicksort
benchmarks.description: Lomuto-partition quicksort with middle-element pivot and recurse-smaller-side / iterate-larger-side, implemented by hand in all three languages so the algorithm itself is identical (complements the stdlib `sort` benchmark).

benchmarks.name: mandelbrot
benchmarks.title: Mandelbrot set (numerical kernel)
benchmarks.description: Compute a Mandelbrot escape-time bitmap of size W*W with up to MAX_ITER iterations. Inspired by the Computer Language Benchmarks Game. Stresses tight numeric loops and floating-point arithmetic.

benchmarks.name: nbody
benchmarks.title: N-Body simulation (numerical kernel)
benchmarks.description: Symplectic integrator for the classic 5-body solar system from the Benchmarks Game over N steps. Stresses tight floating-point loops and array indexing.

benchmarks.name: binary_trees
benchmarks.title: Binary trees (allocation / GC pressure)
benchmarks.description: Build and check many small balanced binary trees up to depth D. Adapted from the Computer Language Benchmarks Game. Stresses small-object allocation and GC (or heap allocator).

benchmarks.name: matrix_multiply
benchmarks.title: Matrix multiplication (naive O(N^3))
benchmarks.description: Compute C = A * B for two NxN double-precision matrices using the textbook triple-loop algorithm. Stresses memory layout, FP multiply-add throughput, and cache behaviour.

benchmarks.name: word_count
benchmarks.title: Word count (text processing)
benchmarks.description: Tokenize a synthesized N-word text and count word frequencies in a hash-map. Stresses string slicing/comparison, hashing, and hash-map updates — a typical scripting workload.

benchmarks.name: spectral_norm
benchmarks.title: Spectral norm (CLBG numerical kernel)
benchmarks.description: Approximates the largest eigenvalue of an infinite matrix A[i][j] = 1 / ((i+j)(i+j+1)/2 + i + 1) via 10 power iterations of v <- A^T A v. Adapted from the Computer Language Benchmarks Game; algorithmically identical across all three languages.

benchmarks.name: bit_count
benchmarks.title: Population-count tight loop (bitwise / integer ops)
benchmarks.description: Compute the population count (Hamming weight) of (i * 2654435761) for i = 0..N-1 via a hand-written 4-operation SWAR popcount kernel that is algorithmically identical across all five languages, and return the total bit count. Stresses bitwise / shift / multiply throughput on 64-bit integers without leaning on each language's stdlib popcount intrinsic.

benchmarks.name: gcd_loop
benchmarks.title: Euclidean GCD tight loop (integer arithmetic)
benchmarks.description: For each i = 1..N, compute gcd((i * 2654435761) mod 10^9, (i * 40503) mod 10^9 + 7) via the iterative Euclidean algorithm, and XOR-fold all results into a checksum. Stresses integer division / modulo throughput in a tight inner loop.

benchmarks.name: xor_shift
benchmarks.title: xorshift64 PRNG tight loop (bit ops + state)
benchmarks.description: Iterate the classic three-shift xorshift64 PRNG N times starting from a fixed seed and return the final state. Pure 64-bit shift / XOR throughput, no memory traffic or stdlib calls.

benchmarks.name: string_split
benchmarks.title: Repeated stdlib String.split
benchmarks.description: Build a fixed comma-separated 64-token string once, then split it REPEATS times using each language's stdlib split, folding the per-iteration token count and selected token length into a checksum. Stresses string parsing and small-array allocation in the standard library.

benchmarks.name: string_search
benchmarks.title: Repeated stdlib substring search (indexOf)
benchmarks.description: Construct a fixed ~10 KB pseudo-random ASCII haystack, then count occurrences of a 5-character needle in a sliding loop using stdlib substring search (indexOf / find / Index), REPEATS times. Stresses string-search throughput without regex.

benchmarks.name: format_loop
benchmarks.title: Integer formatting + string-builder loop
benchmarks.description: Format N integers (zero-padded to width 8) into a single growing string via the language's recommended efficient builder. Stresses integer-to-string formatting and string-buffer growth.

benchmarks.name: set_ops
benchmarks.title: HashSet insert + membership (stdlib)
benchmarks.description: Insert N pseudo-random Int64 values into a hash set, then test membership of N more values from the same stream. Stresses hash-set inserts and lookups (the set-shaped complement to the hashmap_ops benchmark).

benchmarks.name: deque_ops
benchmarks.title: Dynamic-array push/pop tight loop
benchmarks.description: Push N pseudo-random Int64 values onto each language's growable array (Cangjie ArrayList, C++ vector, Rust Vec, Go slice, Python list), then pop them all, XOR-folding popped values into a checksum. Stresses dynamic-array growth and end-removal.

benchmarks.name: conway
benchmarks.title: Conway's Game of Life (cellular automaton)
benchmarks.description: Simulate STEPS generations of Conway's Game of Life on a 200x200 toroidal grid initialised deterministically from an LCG, then count live cells. Stresses tight 2-D array indexing and integer arithmetic.

benchmarks.name: knapsack_dp
benchmarks.title: 0/1 knapsack DP (classic DP)
benchmarks.description: Generate N items with deterministic weights and values from an LCG, then solve the 0/1 knapsack problem with capacity 4000 using a 1-D rolling DP array. Stresses tight integer DP loops and array updates.

benchmarks.name: levenshtein
benchmarks.title: Levenshtein edit-distance DP
benchmarks.description: Compute the Levenshtein edit distance between two deterministic length-L strings drawn from an 8-letter alphabet via two LCG streams, using a 1-D rolling DP. Stresses tight DP inner loops and string indexing.

benchmarks.name: monte_carlo_pi
benchmarks.title: Integer Monte-Carlo PI estimation
benchmarks.description: For N pseudo-random points (x, y) drawn from an LCG modulo R = 65536, count how many satisfy x*x + y*y <= R*R. Pure integer arithmetic, no floating-point, identical algorithm across all languages.

benchmarks.name: histogram
benchmarks.title: Histogram bucketing (data-analysis kernel)
benchmarks.description: Generate N pseudo-random integers via an LCG and bucket each into one of 1024 buckets, returning the XOR-fold of bucket counts. Stresses scatter-style array updates and integer hashing.

benchmarks.name: dijkstra
benchmarks.title: Dense-graph Dijkstra SSSP
benchmarks.description: Build a V*V adjacency matrix with deterministic LCG-derived integer weights, then run Dijkstra's single-source shortest-paths algorithm with an O(V^2) array-based priority. Stresses tight nested integer loops and array indexing.

benchmarks.name: base64
benchmarks.title: Base64 encoder (byte-stream codec)
benchmarks.description: Generate N deterministic bytes via an LCG, then encode them in base64 using a hand-written table-driven encoder, XOR-folding all output bytes into a checksum. Stresses byte-level bitwise operations and array indexing.

benchmarks.name: crc32
benchmarks.title: CRC32 checksum (table-driven hashing)
benchmarks.description: Generate N deterministic bytes via an LCG, then compute the IEEE 802.3 CRC32 byte-by-byte using a precomputed 256-entry lookup table. Identical algorithm across all five languages; stresses tight byte-loop throughput and table lookup.
